messages:
deploy-bot: Canary rollout for `exp-prompt-route:v2` reporting elevated 5xx rate on region-us-east-1 (canary group A) — 5xx ~ 12% over last 3m, latency p95 increased to 2.8s.

sara.w: seeing the same in prod metrics — spike started ~2m after canary push. Not much traffic yet but error budget alerts firing.

ryan-sre: paging oncall @mike_oncall — can you take a look? Logs show `PromptRouter` returning 502 from new endpoint.

mike_oncall: on it. pulling up logs. throwing a quick `curl` at the canary endpoint...

mike_oncall: `curl -i https://canary.exp-route.redwood/v1/prompt` -> 502 with body: `{ "error": "upstream: kvcache-miss -> model-timeout" }`.

thomas: hm recent change in the rollout was the `ff.fastflip.prompt_route` default path -> new proxy that rewrites routing to exp endpoint. Did we enable prefix cache warmup?

elaine_prod: Not for this rollout, we kept warmup off to reduce blast radius.

mike_oncall: can we flip the flag to force traffic to stable path? `ff.fastflip.prompt_route=false`?

elaine_prod: I can toggle. Doing it now in LaunchDarkly UI (targeting canary group A).

elaine_prod: toggled `ff.fastflip.prompt_route` -> false for canary A.

monitoring: :white_check_mark: Rolling count: 5xx rate fell to 4% within 30s. Latency p95 down to 1.1s.

mike_oncall: good, errors dropping. I want to keep it off while we assess. Re-enabling would need careful warmup.

deploy-bot: @incident-bot creating incident record because a feature-flag caused degraded user requests during canary.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2023-1847 created: "Canary: experimental prompt route caused 5xx spike" — severity P2. Pager notify list updated.

ryan-sre: quick customer impact check — any upstream retries or customer-visible failures? I see a short blip of elevated errors on the public API gateway, ~300 requests failed over 10m, mostly from batch ingestion customers.

elaine_prod: flagged top customers with errors: LumaHealth (25 failed requests), Parcelly (18), internal QA harness spiky sends too.

mike_oncall: do we want to abort canary and roll back the deployment entirely or keep disabled flag and let canary continue?

thomas: two risk vectors: 1) code path may still be exercised by other routing logic, 2) if we continue canary without warmup, risk recurring errors. I vote rollback to prev image and re-run with warmup.

sara.w: concur. customer-facing failures albeit small, but we should avoid more. Rollback preference.

elaine_prod: initiating rollback: `deployctl rollback exp-prompt-route v1.9.3` -> starting rollback to stable image.

deploy-bot: Rollback job kicked off: job-id rlb-7732. Expected duration ~4m.

mike_oncall: while rollback runs, I'm going to run a quick regression run against the stable route and verify KV cache behaviour: posting a set of prompts to ensure prefix caching hits.

mike_oncall: regression checks passed on stable route. 200/200 responses, p95 0.45s.

deploy-bot: Rollback completed successfully. Canary instances replaced with stable image. Health checks all green.

monitoring: 5xx rate back to baseline <0.1%, latency to normal.

thomas: great. Incident scope: caused by new proxy rewrite + no cache warmup -> upstream model timeouts under cold KV cache. Follow-ups: require mandatory warmup step for prompt-route canaries OR gradual traffic ramp with KV prefill.

sara.w: add a postmortem and CC product on the decision to skip warmup. Also propose an automated preflight check that simulates prefix traffic.

ryan-sre: tagging owners: @thomas, @elaine_prod for follow-up. I'll create a short RCA doc and a runbook change request.

incident-bot: Updated INC-2023-1847 with notes: rollback performed, FF toggled off during triage, customers notified.

mike_oncall: handing off to @thomas for post-incident follow ups. I'm back on rotation in ~3h.

thomas: taking ownership for follow-ups. immediate actions: 1) add warmup requirement to rollout checklist, 2) add telemetry to flag toggles to show canary impact, 3) schedule a runbook drill.

elaine_prod: sending brief customer notice to affected customers (ops-sre to review) — draft: "We briefly routed canary traffic to an experimental prompt-routing endpoint which caused transient failures; we rolled back and restored normal service. We're implementing guardrails to prevent recurrence."

ops-sre: acknowledged. Please include exact time window and estimated failed request count in the notice.

sara.w: good work triaging quickly. We'll sync in postmortem thread tomorrow with detailed steps and timeline.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2023-1847 marked as RESOLVED (P2) — resolution: rollback + FF set false + customers notified.

mike_oncall: closing my paging loop. If anything else crops up I’ll re-open.

thomas: postmortem task created: PMT-9283. Assigning to @thomas and @ryan-sre.

sara.w: thanks everyone.
